title: Standard course load
text: A standard full-time undergraduate course load is 30 units across the Fall and Winter terms. Students considering more than 30 units should consult their academic advising office before registering.

title: Course overload requests
text: An undergraduate seeking more than 30 units in the Fall and Winter terms must submit an overload request to their Faculty office. Approval may consider academic standing, prior course load, and program requirements.

title: Adding and dropping courses
text: Students may add or drop a Fall or Winter course through the registration system until the published add/drop deadline. After that deadline, registration changes require Faculty approval and may appear as a withdrawal.

title: Prerequisite enforcement
text: A prerequisite is a course or other requirement that must be completed before registration in a subsequent course. The registration system may block enrolment when the prerequisite is not present on the student's record.

title: Permission and prerequisite waivers
text: Permission to register without a listed prerequisite is not automatic. Students must contact the department offering the course, and an approved waiver does not guarantee a seat when the course is full or reserved.

title: Antirequisites
text: Courses listed as antirequisites contain substantial overlapping material. Credit normally may not be retained for both courses, even if they were completed in different academic terms.

title: Repeating a course
text: When an undergraduate repeats a course, both attempts remain on the academic record. The Faculty's academic-standing rules determine how repeated attempts are used in averages and whether additional credit is earned.

title: Course waitlists
text: A place on a course waitlist is not registration in the course. When a seat becomes available, eligible students may receive a time-limited offer according to the department's waitlist procedure.

title: Reserved seating
text: Some course seats are reserved for students in specified programs, levels, or Faculties. Departments may release unused reserved seats later in the registration period, but a release date is not guaranteed.

title: COMPSCI 1MD3 — Introduction to Programming
text: COMPSCI 1MD3 introduces computational problem solving and programming fundamentals. The course carries three units and includes laboratory work. A student should consult the current calendar entry for prerequisites and enrolment restrictions.

title: COMPSCI 2C03 — Data Structures and Algorithms
text: COMPSCI 2C03 covers data structures, algorithm analysis, and implementation. It carries three units and requires COMPSCI 1MD3 or an approved equivalent in this synthetic sample.

title: MATH 1ZA3 — Engineering Mathematics I
text: MATH 1ZA3 is a three-unit introduction to calculus and linear algebra for engineering students. Some seats may be restricted to eligible Engineering programs during initial registration.
